name: Menu
summary: A list of actions behind a trigger button — Snooze presets, 'set stage', row actions. Opens as a non-modal popover, is driven entirely from the keyboard, closes on choice or Escape and returns focus to the trigger. Not for choosing a value (Select, ComboBox) and never for navigation between pages (Link).

pattern.name: Menu Button (menu + menuitem; menuitemradio in single-selection mode)

trigger.intent: The Button that opens the menu. React Aria wires aria-haspopup="menu", aria-expanded and aria-controls onto it. The menu takes its accessible name from this button unless aria-label is given.

children.intent: Items, optionally grouped in sections with a Header. A MenuItem has an id, a visible label, an optional description (Text slot) and an optional keyboard hint (Keyboard slot).

onAction.intent: Fires with the chosen item's id. One handler for the whole menu — the pattern switches on the key ('tomorrow' | '+3d' | 'mon' | 'pick'). React Aria passes the key as the first argument (a second argument may follow); handlers should read only the key.

isOpen.intent: Controlled open state. Pair with onOpenChange. The ActionRow opens the snooze menu from the S key by setting this.

defaultOpen.intent: Uncontrolled initial state. Almost always false.

onOpenChange.intent: Open or closed by any means: trigger press, choice, Escape, Tab out, click outside.

placement.intent: Preferred side and alignment; flips when there is no room. 'end' aligns to the trigger's trailing edge — right for a trigger at the end of a row.

selectionMode.intent: none = actions (menuitem). single = one checked option (menuitemradio with aria-checked) for 'set stage' style menus; the checked item shows a tick AND aria-checked.

selectedKey.intent: single mode only: the checked item. Controlled.

disabledKeys.intent: Items shown but not actionable (aria-disabled, skipped by arrows? No — reachable, announced as dimmed). Prefer hiding an item that can never apply.

aria-label.requiredWhen: the trigger's visible text does not describe the menu (an icon-only '…' trigger).
aria-label.intent: Name of the menu as a whole: 'Snooze until', 'Row actions'.

shouldCloseOnSelect.intent: Close after a choice. false only for multi-step menus, which this product does not have.

keyboard.action: Opens the menu and moves focus to the first item.
Opens the menu and moves focus to the last item.
Move focus between items, wrapping at the ends. Disabled items are reachable and announced as dimmed.
Type-ahead: focus moves to the next item whose label starts with the typed characters.
Activates the focused item (onAction), closes the menu, returns focus to the trigger.
Closes without a choice and returns focus to the trigger.

No effect while the menu is open: the popover is modal for assistive technology (React Aria), focus stays on the current item and the menu stays open. Exits are Escape, a choice, or a click outside — all return focus to the trigger.

a11y.name: The menu is labelled by its trigger (aria-labelledby) — 'Snooze' — or by aria-label when the trigger is an icon. Each item's name is its label text; description and keyboard hint are read after it.
a11y.announcements: Trigger: aria-haspopup="true" (the boolean form React Aria emits — per ARIA it means a menu), aria-expanded true/false. Items: role="menuitem" (menuitemradio + aria-checked in single mode); aria-disabled for disabledKeys. Opening announces the menu's name and the focused item; choosing or Escape returns focus to the trigger, which is announced again. While open, the rest of the page is aria-hidden for assistive technology (modal popover); closing restores it.
a11y.targetSize: Items are 40 px tall (size.target.lg) and span the popover's full width; the trigger is a Button and meets its own size. The popover is at least 160 px wide so short labels are not tiny targets.

rules: Menu is for actions, not values. 'Snooze until…' is a menu; 'Stage: Interview' as a form field is a Select. The role tells a screen-reader user what Enter will do.

The split button (ActionRow's Snooze) is a composition, not a component: a Button that applies the default (+3d) next to a MenuTrigger whose Button is icon-only with aria-label='More snooze options'. Two buttons, two names, one visual group. The pattern owns it.
Focus always returns to the trigger on close — choice, Escape, Tab or click outside (2.4.3). Never leave focus on body.

The menu popover is modal: while open, content outside is hidden from assistive technology and Tab is contained (ADR-029). This is allowed under 2.1.2 because Escape always exits and the exit is in the keyboard map. isNonModal is not used — React Aria warns it degrades the screen-reader experience outside combobox-style components.
The focused item is marked two ways: a background change AND an inset outline ring. The hover background alone is ~1.1:1 against the surface and is not a focus indicator (2.4.7, 1.4.11).
Items hold text, an optional description and an optional keyboard hint — never a nested button, link-button or input. An item that needs a form is a Dialog.
Seven items or fewer in one list; more than that gets sections with headers, or is not a menu.

Destructive actions ('Withdraw application') are plain items that open a confirmation Dialog; no red text in menus — status colours belong to text and rings in the patterns, and one accent per screen.

The popover body uses the same tokens as Card variant='raised' — surface.overlay, border.default, radius.lg — plus shadow.overlay (dark themes drop it through the token); it is not a Card, because a menu's inset is 8 px and Card offers 16 / 24. It renders in a portal at the end of body; no z-index token exists yet — see PARKING.md.

Keyboard hints (Keyboard slot) show the shortcut that triggers the same action outside the menu ('S' for the default snooze). They are informative text, read after the label; they never duplicate the item's name.

properties.Placement: placement (bottom start / bottom end / top start / top end)
properties.Item state: default / hover / focus / active / selected / disabled
